claim_verdicts.source: refs/web/cap-gilbert-lynch.pdf (Gilbert & Lynch, Perspectives on the CAP Theorem; docs root groups.csail.mit.edu/tds/papers/Gilbert/Brewer2.pdf) sec. 1, 2
claim_verdicts.evidence: Key cap_theorem, mirror read. Sec. 2: "In a network subject to communication failures, it is impossible for any web service to implement an atomic read/write shared memory that guarantees a response to every request." Availability: "each request eventually receive a response". Atomic: "as if all the operations were executed by a single centralized server" (= only the latest value). Sec. 1: "it is necessary in practice to sacrifice one of these two desired properties." Key fits.

Both end in failed calls; the lesson no longer says they look the same.

claim_verdicts.source: refs/web/cap-gilbert-lynch.pdf (Gilbert & Lynch, Perspectives on the CAP Theorem; docs root groups.csail.mit.edu/tds/papers/Gilbert/Brewer2.pdf) sec. 2, 4.4
claim_verdicts.evidence: Sec. 2 Partition-tolerance: "a statement regarding the underlying system: communication among the servers is not reliable, and the servers may be partitioned into multiple groups that cannot communicate with each other." Sec. 4.4 Operation partitioning: "Different operations may require different levels of consistency and availability"; "a 'purchase' operation should guarantee consistency, while a 'query' operation might return out of date data." Paper lists operation as one of several dimensions (kind opinion).

claim_verdicts.evidence: Proof sketch: "No matter how long p2 waits, it cannot distinguish these two cases ... It has the choice to either eventually return a response (and risk returning the wrong response) or to never return a response." Sec. 4.1: in one data center "it is only on rare occasions that partitions or other network anomalies occur" - rarer, not absent. Supports both halves.

issues.quote: partition tolerance (the system keeps running through a partition)
issues.text: Gilbert & Lynch sec. 2 frame partition tolerance as an assumption about the network, not a promise of the system: "this property can be seen as a statement regarding the underlying system: communication among the servers is not reliable". 'keeps running through a partition' is a common gloss but reads as a third guarantee the system delivers. Claims 2/4/17 stay verified.
issues.fix: Optional, next content edit: replace the parenthesis with '(the system must work over a network in which partitions can happen)'.
